messages.subject: Drawing rectangles in plot area
parts:
Hi friends, I would like to create following plot, uploaded here:
http://www.2shared.com/photo/jy7p7-0U/plot.html

Here I wanted to create four equally sized rectangles to cover the
entire plot area with different colors. However there should not be
any unused area (unlike that plot in example) in between any
boundaries.

There must be some way out to create the same using ggplot2. I would
be really grateful if someone point me how to do that.

Thanks,

messages.author: 5a1b5a9591c118ef
messages.subject: Re: Drawing rectangles in plot area
parts:
Do you need to use ggplot2 for this?

library(grid)

windowGrob = function(colours, gp = gpar(), vp=NULL, draw=TRUE, ...) {

fillm = matrix(colours, ncol= n2mfrow(length(colours))[2] )

g = rasterGrob(fillm, x = unit(0.5, "npc"), y = unit(0.5,
"npc"), width = unit(1, "npc"), height = unit(1,
"npc"),..., interpolate=FALSE,
gp = gp, vp = vp)

if (draw) grid.draw(g)
invisible(g)
}

windowGrob(palette()[1:4])


HTH,

baptiste

messages.subject: Re: Drawing rectangles in plot area
parts:
You can do it with geom_tile,


d = expand.grid(x = 1:2, y = 1:2)
d$fill = seq(1, nrow(d))

qplot(x,y, data=d,fill=fill, geom="tile")

HTH,

baptiste
